title: The Orchard of Port Alder
premise: Jonah Halloran ghostwrites the memoirs of shipping magnate Charles Vane in the fading coastal town of Port Alder, hiding behind other people's words since a betrayal ended his engagement ten years ago. When Mara Ellison — the woman who wrote him anonymous letters through his worst decade, whom he's loved without ever meeting — moves into the cottage next door, he discovers she is Vane's estranged daughter and the memoirs are being shaped to erase her. Torn between his contract, his growing love for Mara, and his own complicity in rewriting lives, Jonah must expose the manuscript's lies and forgive himself for abandoning his own story. On the last ferry of the season, he chooses truth over duty, and Mara chooses him.
about_author: Rosalind Okafor is a former maritime archivist who spent five years cataloguing letters in coastal town libraries before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted boathouse on the Atlantic seaboard, where she collects unsent correspondence.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He arrives in Port Alder to ghostwrite Charles Vane's memoirs, drafting flattering lies about a decades-old business scandal. Establishes his habit of living in past tense. Emotional beat: quiet self-erasure, a man fluent in everyone's voice but his own.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Jonah's POV. Reveals the anonymous letters that sustained him after his broken engagement — signed only 'M.' He never answered the last one. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with cowardice; love kept safely hypothetical.

chapters.title: The Woman Next Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She moves into the neighboring cottage with boxes of her mother's papers, wary of her father's town. She notices the light burning late next door. Emotional beat: guarded hope, returning to a place that remembers her.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Talk
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jonah and Mara meet at the harbor market; instant, uncomfortable recognition of something familiar in each other. Neither names it. Emotional beat: the shock of near-recognition, chemistry neither can afford.

chapters.title: Vane's Version
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Charles Vane dictates a chapter painting his daughter as the villain of the family rupture. Jonah writes it down, hating himself. Emotional beat: complicity; the first crack between Jonah's conscience and his contract.

chapters.title: The Orchard Gate
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She restores her grandmother's abandoned orchard and finds Jonah repairing the shared fence line unasked. First real conversation. Emotional beat: two lonely people discovering ease in each other's company.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He finds one of Mara's old letters washed from a flooded storage unit — her handwriting matches 'M.' He says nothing, terrified of being wrong and more terrified of being right. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past tense collapsing.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Harbor House
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vane hosts a strained family dinner where Jonah, as 'the biographer,' watches Mara dismantle her father's mythology over dessert. Emotional beat: admiration curdling into dread as Jonah realizes whose story he's been selling.

chapters.title: The Draft That Lies
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Rereading the manuscript, he sees how systematically it erases Mara. His editor warns him: deliver on time or lose everything. Emotional beat: the mirror moment — he recognizes his own betrayals in Vane's revisions.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A storm strands Jonah at her cottage; they talk until dawn about second chances without revealing what they know. Emotional beat: intimacy achieved through almost-confession, the letters hovering unspoken between them.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. On Mara's porch, on the edge of kissing her, he pulls back — still bound by the manuscript, still hiding. She reads it as rejection. Emotional beat: heartbreak by hesitation; the cost of half-truths.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She learns the last ferry of the season runs in three weeks, then finds a copy of Vane's draft pages in Jonah's recycling — her own life, falsified. Emotional beat: betrayal layered on longing; she assumes Jonah wrote the lies willingly.

chapters.title: Cold Water
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Mara confronts Jonah coldly; he can't explain without breaking confidentiality. The fence between their yards becomes a real boundary again. Emotional beat: silence as self-protection, both retreating into old wounds.

chapters.title: Charles Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Alone, he rereads his late wife's letters and admits the memoir is revenge against a daughter who saw through him. He pressures Jonah to finish by ferry day. Emotional beat: power corrupting even its holder; loneliness dressed as authority.

chapters.title: The Unsent Reply
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He finally writes the answer to 'M.' he never sent ten years ago — not knowing if she'll ever read it. Emotional beat: catharsis; forgiving the person in the mirror begins with telling the truth on paper.

chapters.title: Discovery in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Restoring the orchard, she finds her mother's hidden letters proving Vane manufactured the family scandal. She realizes the memoir isn't just cruel — it's false. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Vane offers him double pay to bury the truth and hints he'll ruin Mara legally. Jonah refuses, walks out with the manuscript, and slides the unsent reply under Mara's door. Emotional beat: the break — choosing love and integrity over safety.

chapters.title: Reading by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She reads his letter, understands ten years of silence, and finds the true letters that could destroy her father's book. But trusting Jonah again means risking everything twice. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered, not yet accepted.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Approaches
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. Jonah prepares to publish the truth independently; Vane threatens litigation; Mara must decide whether to stand beside him or leave on the morning boat. Emotional beat: rising dread, all threads tightening toward departure day.

chapters.title: Ferry Day
chapters.summary: Climax, both POVs. At the dock, Vane publicly accuses Jonah of theft; Mara steps forward with her mother's letters and claims her own story aloud. Vane falters before the town. The ferry sounds its horn. Emotional beat: confrontation, public truth, love declared against duty.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Aftermath: Vane withdraws the memoir rather than face exposure; Jonah publishes nothing but gives Mara every page — her story, hers to tell. They plant the orchard's first new tree together. Emotional beat: release; belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: First Person, Present Tense
chapters.summary: Mara's closing POV, shifting to present tense. Spring returns; she begins writing her own memoir in her own voice, with Jonah beside her as reader, not ghost. The ferry returns with the season. Emotional beat: resolution — love in present tense at last.
